title: paw-fx effect meta
description: meta.json for one effect under effects/<name>/. Validated by scripts/lint.mjs. origin is always required; repo, commit and path inside it are required only for a ported effect, which is why they live in the else branch and not in properties.origin -- listing them there made the paw-fx carve-out dead and forced originals to ship an empty commit.

category.description: Which shelf the effect sits on. `menu` covers navigation reveals and hover treatments on nav items; `gallery` covers image grids, sliders and looping galleries. Both were added when the Codrops survey found its two strongest families had nowhere to go. `character` covers a mascot or avatar the page drives by state rather than a decorative background.

commit.description: A real resolved commit sha, never a branch or tag name. The gate fetches this exact commit.

path.description: The upstream file this effect is ported from. A LIST when the port genuinely spans several upstream files: a paper-design shader splices in shader-utils.ts and shader-sizing.ts, every vanta effect extends src/_base.js, and the marquee needs its component plus the globals.css that defines its keyframes. Listing them all is what stops the port-fidelity gate reading shared upstream code as invention.

url.description: The source page the code was taken from. Used with the snapshot shape.

retrieved.description: The date the snapshot was taken, ISO. A snapshot source can change under us, so when we looked is part of the record.

sha256.description: Hash of the committed snapshot file, which is what the gate verifies against.

snapshot.description: Repo-relative path to the committed copy of the upstream source. Pin the extracted author panels, not a wrapper page: a host's wrapper carries content-hashed asset URLs and injected runtime guards, so hashing it false-fails on the host's own churn and diffs against code the author never wrote.

origin.description: Where the effect was ported from. Two shapes are allowed, because not every usable source is a git repository. A git origin is repo + commit + path, and the gate re-fetches that exact commit. A snapshot origin is url + retrieved + sha256 + snapshot, for a source with no commit to pin, such as a CodePen the author can edit at any time with no version history. There the pinned reference is a copy of the source committed alongside the effect, and the gate compares its hash. Both are real provenance; they are anchored differently.

deviations.description: Deliberate, declared departures from upstream. The port-fidelity gate treats an undeclared change to shader source, easing curves or timing constants as invention and fails it; declaring it here with a reason is how a necessary change passes. Use `kind` to say which sort it is.

kind.description: seam = plumbing we always change. upstream-bug = broken at the pinned commit itself, so fixing it is not a migration. api-migration = a dependency version forced it. ours = a deliberate product choice, which must be justified.
